findings.passage: “This is not a partisan or political issue. Voter ID laws are overwhelmingly popular, and for good reason,” Martin said. “Requiring voters to prove who they are before they cast their ballot is one of the most effective ways to reduce fraud, strengthen the integrity of our elections and instill more confidence in the system.”
findings.note: Quoted by ABC12 (WJRT) after the House passed Senate Bills 303 and 304, which require a photo ID at the polls, with a provisional ballot cured by showing ID to the clerk within six days. Date is the page's published date.

findings.passage: “Making it completely free to get a state ID card will eliminate any possibility that cost or access to identification would prevent someone from voting,” Martin said. “Every single Michigander will still be able to exercise their right and have their voice heard at the ballot box.”
findings.note: Quoted by ABC12 (WJRT) on House Bill 5007, which waives the $10 state ID fee for eligible people.

findings.passage: “Our vote is our voice, and ensuring our vote counts is a crucial part of having confidence in our elections. That’s why Dave voted for strengthening ID requirements when voting in-person or by absentee ballot (SB 285). Dave supported legislation to prohibit the Secretary of State from sending unrequested absentee ballots applications (SB 310) and voted for legislation to require a physical signature when requesting an absentee ballot (HB 5288).”
findings.note: His answer in Ballotpedia's candidate survey, as excerpted by Ballotpedia news (written in the third person). Covers ID for in-person and absentee voting, unrequested absentee applications, and a signature to request an absentee ballot.
